title: 1999 AHSME Problem 18
statement: How many zeros does \(f(x) = \cos(\log x)\) have on the interval \(0 \lt x \lt 1?\)

solutions.text:
As \(x\) ranges over \((0, 1),\) \(\log x\) ranges over all negative real numbers. The cosine function is zero at \(\tfrac{\pi}{2} - n\pi\) for every positive integer \(n,\) all of which are negative, so \(f\) has infinitely many zeros.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: As \(x\) ranges over \((0, 1),\) what values does \(\log x\) take?
\(\log x\) covers all negative numbers, and cosine vanishes at infinitely many of them
